drivingQuestion: Which tanna holds that slaughter requires no intent, and how can a knife thrown at a wall effect valid slaughter?
outcomeNote: The mishna is identified with R' Natan, who does not require intent, and the objection from the requirement of a back-and-forth motion is answered by a knife that both went and returned

segments.he: אָמַר רָבָא: רַבִּי נָתָן הִיא, דְּתָנֵי אוֹשַׁעְיָא זְעֵירָא דְּמִן חַבְרַיָּא: זָרַק סַכִּין לְנוֹעֳצָהּ בַּכּוֹתֶל, וְהָלְכָה וְשָׁחֲטָה כְּדַרְכָּהּ – רַבִּי נָתָן מַכְשִׁיר, וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹסְלִין. הוּא תָּנֵי לַהּ, וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי נָתָן.
segments.en: «Rava said:» It «is Rabbi Natan, as Oshaya, the youngest of the company» of Sages, «taught» a baraita, stating: If «one threw a knife to embed it in the wall, and» in the course of its flight the knife «went and slaughtered» an animal «in its» proper «manner, Rabbi Natan deems» the slaughter «valid, and the Rabbis deem» the slaughter «not valid.» Oshaya «teaches» the baraita «and he states about it: The halakha is in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Natan» that there is no need for intent to perform a valid act of slaughter.

segments.he: וְהָא בָּעֵינַן מוֹלִיךְ וּמֵבִיא? שֶׁהָלְכָה וּבָאָה כְּדַרְכָּהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: How could the slaughter in the baraita be valid? «But don’t we require» that the slaughterer «move» the knife «back and forth» on the throat of the animal? When one throws a knife, it goes in one direction and does not return. The Gemara answers: The case in the baraita is one «where the knife went» and cut the animal’s throat, caromed off the wall «and came» back to cut the throat again «in its» proper «manner.»
